title: Power Outage Indicator
shortDescription: The refrigerator detected a power interruption.
fullDescription:
PO flashes on Jenn-Air refrigerators after a power outage has occurred. It signals the freezer temperature may have risen during the outage. Check food safety — foods above 40F for over 2 hours should be discarded.

Press any pad to clear the PO indicator. The unit resumes normal operation automatically.
symptoms: Food may be warmer than normal

fixSteps.title: Clear indicator
fixSteps.instruction: Press any button on the control panel to acknowledge.

fixSteps.title: Check food safety
fixSteps.instruction: Verify freezer still at 0F, fridge below 40F. Discard spoiled items.

fixSteps.title: Secure outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure plug is fully seated and outlet is not GFCI-tripped.

whenToCallPro: Only if outlet issues persist — call an electrician.
videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air refrigerator PO power outage clear

faq.a: Refrigerated food over 40F for 2+ hours should be discarded; frozen food with ice crystals can be refrozen.

title: Fresh Food Thermistor Fault
shortDescription: The refrigerator compartment temperature sensor is failing.
fullDescription:
E1 indicates the fresh food thermistor is out of range. This NTC thermistor monitors refrigerator temperature; without it, cooling cannot be properly regulated.

Replacement is straightforward — the thermistor clips inside the fresh-food compartment near the top.
symptoms: Fresh food too warm or too cold

fixSteps.title: Locate thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Found in fresh food section, near top rear wall.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Unclip old thermistor, install new, reseat plug.

faq.q: Why does fridge still run with E1?
faq.a: The board uses last-known-good setpoint — cooling continues but is not optimized.

title: Freezer Thermistor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer compartment temperature sensor is failing.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the freezer thermistor is reporting invalid values. Located near the evaporator in the freezer section, this sensor allows the control to regulate freezer temp and defrost timing.

A stuck-high reading will cause the compressor to run continuously; stuck-low will cause warm freezer.

fixSteps.title: Access evaporator cover
fixSteps.instruction: Remove freezer rear panel to expose coil and thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clip onto evaporator tube, reseat connector.

whenToCallPro: If heavy ice buildup blocks access to the panel.

faq.a: Yes — defrost the unit overnight before working on the evaporator area.

title: Defrost System Fault
shortDescription: The defrost cycle did not complete successfully.
fullDescription:
E3 means the control did not see the expected evaporator temperature rise during a defrost cycle, indicating heater or terminator failure. Without proper defrost, frost accumulates on the evaporator, reducing cooling.

Test heater and defrost terminator with a multimeter. Both must show continuity at cold temperatures.

fixSteps.title: Defrost unit
fixSteps.instruction: Empty, unplug 24h to clear existing frost.

fixSteps.title: Test components
fixSteps.instruction: Heater should read 20-40Ω; bimetal should be closed at cold.

fixSteps.title: Replace part
fixSteps.instruction: Install new heater or bimetal as indicated.

whenToCallPro: If unfamiliar with refrigerator evaporator servicing.

title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: The freezer evaporator fan has failed.
fullDescription:
E4 indicates the evaporator fan motor isn't running or isn't reporting proper RPM feedback. This fan circulates cold air from the evaporator throughout both compartments.

Ice buildup can block the blade — defrost and inspect before replacing parts.

fixSteps.title: Listen for fan
fixSteps.instruction: With door switch depressed by hand, fan should run.

fixSteps.title: Check for ice
fixSteps.instruction: Defrost if blade is frozen. Investigate defrost system if so.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove evaporator cover, swap fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If defrost issue coexists and you're uncomfortable with multiple repairs.
videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air refrigerator E4 evaporator fan fix

faq.q: Why doesn't fan run with door open?
faq.a: Door switch stops fan when door opens to save energy.

title: Condenser Fan Fault
shortDescription: The condenser fan below the unit has failed.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates the condenser fan motor isn't running. This fan cools the compressor and condenser coil; without it, high-side pressure rises and the compressor overheats.

Access is typically from the lower rear — pull the refrigerator out to service.

fixSteps.title: Clean area
fixSteps.instruction: Pull unit, vacuum dust, clear debris from fan blade.

fixSteps.title: Spin fan
fixSteps.instruction: Blade should spin freely by hand.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove fan from bracket, install new motor.

whenToCallPro: If unit cannot be pulled out due to flooring or built-in trim.
videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air refrigerator E5 condenser fan fix

faq.q: Can I run without the condenser fan?
faq.a: No — the compressor will overheat and fail.

title: Freezer Door Open
shortDescription: The freezer door has been open too long.
fullDescription:
Fd alert displays when the freezer door has been open beyond the alarm threshold (typically 5 minutes). An audible tone accompanies the alert. Close the door or dismiss by pressing a button.

Persistent Fd with closed door indicates a failed door switch.

fixSteps.title: Close door
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure freezer drawer/door is fully closed and seal is intact.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Press switch plunger or test reed switch with magnet.

videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air refrigerator Fd door alert fix

faq.a: Press any control pad to mute for 10 minutes.

title: Over-Current Protection
shortDescription: Excess current draw detected on a load.
fullDescription:
OC indicates the control tripped overcurrent protection on one of the loads (compressor, heater, fan, ice maker). The board disables power to prevent damage.

Inspect each load to isolate which is drawing too much current. A shorted motor winding or heater is typical.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power; inspect each load for shorts.

fixSteps.title: Resistance check
fixSteps.instruction: Measure each motor and heater resistance vs service chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace shorted part
fixSteps.instruction: Install new component; do not bypass OC protection.

whenToCallPro: Strongly recommended — shorted components can be hard to identify without experience.

faq.a: Keep the unit unplugged until diagnosed to avoid further damage.

title: Display Test or Stuck Segments
shortDescription: All display segments lit — test pattern or failure.
fullDescription:
An '88' reading with all segments illuminated indicates either a self-test mode at power-up (normal for 3-5 seconds) or stuck segments indicating display board failure if persistent.

If 88 persists after power cycle, replace the display board.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 5 minutes, restore. Self-test ends within seconds.

faq.a: Not always — it's also the self-test pattern. Only a concern if stuck for more than a minute.

title: Fast Freeze Mode Active
shortDescription: Fast freeze boost mode is running.
fullDescription:
FF is a status indicator (not an error) showing the Fast Freeze feature is active. In this mode, the compressor runs continuously for up to 24 hours to quickly freeze newly-added items.

FF turns off automatically after the cycle. If FF is stuck on, try manually disabling via the control or power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Disable manually
fixSteps.instruction: Press Fast Freeze pad to toggle off.

faq.a: Yes — expect elevated energy use during the 24h cycle.

title: System Communication Error
shortDescription: Internal communication between control boards has failed.
fullDescription:
SY (often shown as SY CE) indicates system communication error — the main control board cannot reach another subsystem board (display, dispenser, ice maker, etc.) over the data bus.

Check harness connections first. Persistent SY requires board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harnesses
fixSteps.instruction: Check communication cables at each board.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Install new control board as diagnosed.

whenToCallPro: Board diagnosis is tricky without service bulletins.
